headline: High risk of prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors from shared filesystem plus broad network/tool access in Roo Code and Mentat.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Mentat and Roo Code both share state via filesystem, and Roo Code can ingest workspace files plus browser screenshots while Mentat reads/writes selected files. That creates a plausible content-to-instruction bridge if one agent processes the other's outputs as trusted text. No MCP bridge is documented for Mentat, so this is not high.
conditions: IF either agent reads the other agent's generated files as instructions without provenance checks
IF a shared workspace is used for handoff between the two agents
mitigations: Separate their working directories
Require a human review step before one agent consumes the other's output
Prefix generated artifacts with machine-readable provenance headers
Disable automatic ingestion of shared files
requires-engineering: add provenance-aware parsing between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents touch source code and share state via filesystem, so sensitive code can flow between them through the workspace. Roo Code also calls configured model APIs and MCP servers, increasing the chance that shared file contents leave the local environment. Mentat likewise calls a model provider API, so leakage can occur from either side.
conditions: IF sensitive source files are present in the shared workspace
IF either agent forwards workspace contents to its configured model backend or MCP server
mitigations: Use separate workspaces for sensitive files
Restrict both agents to non-sensitive repositories
Turn off MCP servers for Roo Code during shared work
Review outbound API destinations before running
requires-engineering: add per-file redaction before model calls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have unrestricted filesystem write, read, and modify_git_state, and both share state via filesystem. Roo Code additionally has shell, subprocess, and browser capabilities, so concurrent edits can race and corrupt git state or workspace files. Mentat's diff-based edits do not prevent conflicts when both write the same tree.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git checkout or workspace directory
IF edits are made concurrently or without external locking
mitigations: Run only one agent per workspace
Serialize edits with a lock file
Commit after each agent's turn
Use separate git branches
requires-engineering: add workspace-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Mentat produces diff-based edit proposals, and Roo Code can act across shell, browser, and MCP surfaces. If Roo Code treats Mentat's output as authoritative, an error or hallucination can cascade into real actions or commits. The reverse path is also plausible because both agents can modify files and git state.
conditions: IF Roo Code applies Mentat-generated diffs without independent verification
IF either agent uses the other's output as a direct action plan
mitigations: Require explicit human approval before applying diffs
Compare proposed changes against tests before execution
Limit Roo Code to read-only review when consuming Mentat output
Ask both agents to cite file-level evidence for claims
requires-engineering: add automated diff validation

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source coding assistants with no explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch documented. The main compliance concern is that both handle source code and model-provider API keys, but the profiles do not show a cross-border or regulated-data violation. Mentat is not cited separately for residency because none is specified.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is placed in the shared workspace
IF the configured model providers retain prompts contrary to policy
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both tools
Review provider retention settings
Use separate projects for sensitive work
Document data handling expectations for operators
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for prompt retention
